results.answer: The Caesar cipher shifts every letter of the alphabet by a fixed number of places [1]. With a shift of 3, A becomes D and B becomes E [1]. The Vigenère cipher uses a keyword to choose a different Caesar shift for each letter [2]. The keyword repeats along the message, so the same plain letter can encrypt to different cipher letters [2].

The rail fence cipher is a transposition cipher [1]. It writes the message in a zigzag across a number of rails and reads the rows one after another [1]. The rail fence cipher does not change the letters, only their order, so letter frequencies stay the same as in the plain text [2].

The Vigenère cipher uses a keyword to choose a different Caesar shift for each letter [1]. The keyword repeats along the message, so the same plain letter can encrypt to different cipher letters [1]. The Vigenère cipher resists simple frequency analysis better than the Caesar cipher because letter frequencies are flattened [2]. It can still be broken by finding the key length and then attacking each position like a Caesar cipher [2].
